summary.headline: JK Cement Q1 FY27 standalone net sales rose 23% YoY to INR3,786 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.9% from 21.9% on cost pressure.
summary.overview: Grey cement volumes grew 19% YoY and white/putty volumes 11%, driving combined volume growth of 18% YoY (down 3% QoQ). Standalone EBITDA was INR639 crore (INR982/ton) versus INR673 crore a year earlier, with margin compressed by fuel and maintenance costs. Management guided to a further ~INR150/ton cost increase in Q2 driven mainly by fuel, and reiterated capacity expansion timelines (Jaisalmer in 1H FY28) with no deferral. Net debt rose to INR3,864 crore from INR3,370 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Grey cement
segments.commentary: Volumes up 19% YoY and down 2% QoQ; growth driven by Central India expansion including the Bihar grinding unit, while North and South grew only in line with market.

segments.name: White cement and putty
segments.commentary: Volumes up 11% YoY and down 5% QoQ; benefited from reduced UAE imports due to the geopolitical situation, but management expects competition to normalise.

segments.name: Paints (Acro and Maxx brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR125 crore in Q1 at EBITDA breakeven, versus about INR100 crore in each of the prior three quarters; FY27 revenue target INR500-550 crore; capex capped at INR600 crore.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR35-40 crore versus about INR5 crore in Q4 FY26; 17 plants operative; target about INR250 crore revenue in FY27 with EBITDA near breakeven (single-digit loss), and 4-7% margin at maturity.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 per-ton cost to rise about INR150, of which about INR100 is fuel and about INR50 diesel/other; packaging flat to marginally lower; maintenance similar or marginally lower.
Full-year FY27 grey volume target of 22.5-23 million tonnes, implying double-digit growth but a slower run-rate in the remaining quarters.
FY27 capex about INR3,500 crore and FY28 about INR1,200 crore, excluding any next expansion phase.
Incentive income FY29 expected at INR225-250 crore due to input credit constraints, rising to about INR300 crore annually once GST-linked subsidy is restored.
Paint business targeted at about 5-7% EBITDA margin in FY28 with revenue up about INR150 crore.
capex_capacity: Jaisalmer greenfield project on track for commissioning in 1H FY28; Bhatinda grinding unit progressing; second Punjab grinding site land acquired.
Nathdwara putty capacity expansion (0.6 MTPA) expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; Rajasthan putty expansion near completion.
Panna Line 2 clinker to be debottlenecked from 3.3 to 4 million tonnes within FY27; Panna overall utilisation above 65%.

Effective utilisation in the North and South regions about 85-90%; expansion to 40 MTPA in FY28 and 50 MTPA by 2030 with no deferral; next clinker line (Muddapur as next priority) decision expected around end-FY27.
Mahan coal block expected to start supplying coal by end-FY28, with the second block about one year later; coal from captive blocks expected to be substantially cheaper.
demand_pricing: Prices flat QoQ in the monsoon quarter on average; management expects no price drop despite low seasonal volumes given cost pressures.

Q1 fuel mix was 40% petcoke, 45% Indian coal and balance alternate fuels; Central India runs on domestic fuel only, while North plants use Indian coal (rail-linked) and petcoke, and South uses only petcoke and alternate fuels.
Fuel cost per kcal expected around 1.75 in Q2 versus 1.53 in Q1, peaking in Q2 before declining.
White cement exports from UAE (Fujairah) restricted to GCC; about 50% of normal UAE volume lost in Q1 due to shipping constraints.
Consolidated raw material cost per ton higher partly because dry-mix mortar in UAE is included in consolidated numerator but not in volume denominator.

qa_highlights.question: How much of volume growth came from new capacity and how are regions performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly from Central India expansion including Bihar grinding unit; North and South grew only with the market as no spare volume is available there; some market share gained in Central India.

qa_highlights.question: How much will costs rise in Q2 and is this the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-ton cost up about INR150 in Q2 (INR100 fuel, INR50 diesel/other); Q2 expected to be the fuel cost peak; maintenance flat to marginally lower in Q2 with about INR50-60 crore pre-poned from Q2 into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Are expansion plans being delayed given industry capacity pullbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: No; on schedule with 40 MTPA in FY28 and 50 MTPA by 2030; next-phase Board approval timing not yet fixed given geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth of 16-17% be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan for 22.5-23 MTPA in FY27 implying double-digit growth; sustainability depends on demand and capacity in North and South, which are constrained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did white cement volumes rise so sharply and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Reduced UAE imports during the geopolitical situation opened extra volume; management expects competition in white and putty to continue once markets normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook versus prior incremental volume guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it revises the annual number every quarter, will maximise volumes, and will avoid aggressive price-led growth; growth in North and South is capacity-limited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR3,500 crore in FY27 and about INR1,200 crore in FY28, excluding the next expansion leg.

risks_watch: Fuel cost inflation (petcoke, diesel) with Q2 cost up about INR150/ton; fuel cost per kcal expected near 1.75 in Q2.
Net debt rose to INR3,864 crore with capex of about INR3,500 crore in FY27, keeping leverage under watch.
Capacity constraints in North and South limit volume growth; FY27 volume target implies slower growth in the remaining three quarters.
Thermal substitution target of 35% by FY30 is being reworked; current rate around 11-12%. Green power target of 75% depends on pending state approvals.
Geopolitical risk to UAE white cement exports and to Middle East shipping; FY29 incentive income depends on GST subsidy restoration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and expansion schedule, but cautious on cost and geopolitics; management declined to share regional profitability or utilisation, and was non-committal on the timing of the next expansion Board approval.
